newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks comment on food labeling proposals.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks comment on food labeling proposals.

text.p: The Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service said Friday it was seeking public comment on possible alternatives to regulations determining the composition and name of many foods.

"We want to know what people think about the relevance and usefulness of current standards of identity and composition for meat and poultry products," said USDA acting undersecretary for Food Safety Michael Taylor.
The safety of consumers would not be compromised but some current standards might impede innovation and slow the introduction of products with reduced fat and cholesterol, a statement said.
A notice of the proposed rulemaking is due to be published in the Federal Register on Monday.
"We don't want our labeling rules to limit the flexibility companies need to produce nutritionally improved meat and poultry products," Taylor said.
